items.reason: The gap is not present: all 19 live `${{ }}` expressions in agent-review.yml are `env:` bindings (verified line by line), no `run:` body interpolates one, and scripts/actions-pin.mjs rules P5/P7 already block this repo-wide as a required check — the scan's hit is one of three comment lines that quote the hazard in prose (agent-review.yml:70, :123 and agent-review-history.yml:46), and rewording those would be editing a file to satisfy a detector; I added the missing verification test instead.

Needs network: pinning the 25 action refs and the Dockerfile's 3 `FROM node:24-alpine` stages means asking GitHub/the registry what each tag points at right now, and inventing a SHA breaks the workflow rather than pinning it — everything else the close needs is already in the tree (`npm run actions:pin --update` rewrites the refs and flips STRICT/RATCHET in one pass, and Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem is already enabled), so this is one networked command by a human, not a missing practice.

lessons: This repository pairs every blocking policy rule with an independent unit test that restates the rule's own list (test-unit/workflow-triggers.test.mjs does it for actions-pin.mjs P2), on the reasoning that the cheap way to reintroduce a class is to delete the rule rather than to write a violation. When a security item here looks already-fixed, check whether the FENCE is pinned by a test before concluding there is nothing to do — that was the only real gap behind the agent-review.yml finding.

Scanners that flag .github/workflows here will produce false positives, because these workflows document the hazard they defend against in prose that quotes it (`${{ … }}`, `run:`, `pull_request_target` all appear in comments). The repo's own scripts strip comment lines before matching and say so explicitly; an external scan that does not will keep re-raising a closed gap, and the right answer is a skip with the line numbers, not a reworded comment.

scripts/actions-pin.mjs P8 claims 'there are no container images in this repository today', but the Dockerfile's three `FROM node:24-alpine` stages are outside the script's scope (it only reads .github/workflows). Worth closing when someone can run the networked pin — the base image floats across every 24.x patch, which is looser than any action ref here.
